`data/E1_DERIVATION.json`, `data/E1_BOARDS.json` and `data/E1_FOCUS.json`.

Every check is paired with an input that must make it fail. A check proved only by the

## 2. Layers

**Layer A — pure Node. Runs from a bare extraction with no project root, no siblings and no browser.** 25 checks.

**Layer B — needs the rendered boards.** 4 checks.

**Layer C — needs Chrome.** 3 checks.

## 4. The probes

**R01** *a state token aliasing the identity material* — FIRED. qandeel.state.selected.marker -> qandeel.identity.material -> qandeel.expression.material.living-brass.body

**R02** *a hue given to the selection marker* — FIRED. the check would report ["qandeel.state.selected.marker"] under qandeel.state and fail

**R03** *a role given a hue by taxonomy — declared nowhere, earned nowhere, and simply aliased* — FIRED. the graph would reach a status literal for ["error","warning"] while the shipped policy declares ["error"] — a hue that nobody wrote down as earned is rejected, which is the OTHER direction of REV-03: removing the cap must not remove the discipline

**R04** *a token path with no classification* — FIRED. e1-tokens: token "qandeel.state.hover.ink" carries no freeze classification. Classify it or do not ship it.

**R05** *a token group actually named accent* — FIRED. [".qandeel.state.accent"]

**R06** *the retired literal used as a value* — FIRED. a probe document containing it as a value is rejected by the count rule

**R07** *an E1 token written into the frozen content ramp* — FIRED. qandeel.expression.content.quaternary would be rejected

**R08** *resolving WITHOUT E1’s file* — FIRED. C3 alone still says: RESERVED AND DELIBERATELY EMPTY. Interaction state exp...

**R09** *a disabled ink only just below the tertiary* — FIRED. #7f7d77 sits only 0.0401 below

**R10** *dropping the companion* — FIRED. without it the indicator fails 3:1 against PRIMARY, SECONDARY, TERTIARY, BRASS, LIGHT-low, LIGHT-mid, LIGHT-core, ERROR

**R11** *a press wash pointed at QANDEEL LIGHT* — FIRED. qandeel.state.pressed.ink -> qandeel.illumination.core -> qandeel.expression.illumination.core is rejected by the chain rule — and note it composites to #2f2e2c, chroma 0.00383, which a chroma ceiling would have WAVED THROUGH

**R12** *a press alpha that produces the Surface value exactly* — FIRED. alpha 0.041 would collide and this check would reject it

**R13** *a more chromatic value elsewhere in the system* — FIRED. the most chromatic would become FAKE

**R14** *the IDENTICAL floors applied to two error reds nobody derived against THIS palette* — FIRED. Material 3 dark error #f2b8b5: 3 floors unmet — protan: dEok from LIGHT-low 0.0419 < 0.051294338032078474; deutan: dEok from PRIMARY 0.0406 < 0.051294338032078474; deutan: dEok from LIGHT-low 0.0181 < 0.051294338032078474  ||  Apple systemRed dark #ff453a: 2 floors unmet — protan: contrast on WORLD 3.7436 < 4.5; protan: contrast on SURFACE 3.4934 < 4.5  — the floors are specific to THIS palette, not a generic bar, which is why E1 derived a value instead of adopting one

**R15** *the C1R statement, which is about the Brass MARK and is not measured here* — FIRED. C1R: "a disabled item whose mark is at full material strength does not look disabled at a glance". E1 resolves it by ruling the case out of the product, not by measurement — and says so.

**R16** *a corrupted vendored copy* — FIRED. one trailing byte changes the digest, and the check compares digests

**R17** *the dark values copied into the light set — the corruption an implementer actually commits, because "it looks fine"* — FIRED. a light set carrying #fe907e would be a light-mode error colour invented by accident; every floor that produced it is a statement about a NEAR-BLACK ground

**R18** *the tritan limit, asserted as a check rather than discovered by a reviewer* — FIRED. moved 0.00001; tritan is EXCLUDED from every derived floor

**R26** *I-08B3.1-E1’s own frozen absolute, fed back in: a single pattern in which unavailable always means unfocusable* — FIRED. one pattern, focusable=false for every unavailable control — this is exactly what E1 froze, and the check rejects it. W3C APG: screen reader users are far less likely to discover disabled elements that are not focusable, because moving focus is one of their primary methods of discovery

**R32** *the combination declared impossible everywhere at once, with no control type named* — FIRED. a single blanket row with no proof is rejected on three counts at once: too few control types, no proof, and a global claim

**R27** *a combination left undefined — the gap the old model hid by declaring one of them impossible* — FIRED. removing focus+disabled leaves ["focus+disabled"] undefined, and the check fails — which is the state I-08B3.1-E1 shipped in, with that combination recorded as "cannot occur"

**R28** *the ownership table asserting exclusivity the matrix contradicts — the exact shape of the withdrawn claim* — FIRED. the shipped matrix has ["selected","disabled"] writing the INK channel; a model declaring only ["selected"] is rejected. This is not a hypothetical: it is what the package shipped, stated as a frozen Product contract

**R29** *the cap sentence I-08B3.1-E1 actually froze, put back into the shipped contract list* — FIRED. restoring E1’s statement 9 makes this check fail — the cap is detected in the token document that ships, not in a guard’s prose

**R30** *the rule I-08B3.1-E1 SHIPPED — the navigation icon repainted to the unavailable ink when the item became unavailable* — FIRED. both are caught: .navitem[data-state~="disabled"] .ic and .ctl[data-state~="disabled"]. The first is not invented — it was in the stylesheet for the whole of E1, two packages after the material’s state-invariance was frozen, because a universal law had made it unreachable and therefore unexamined

**R25** *a scene holding one hex of its own* — FIRED. even a literal that happens to be CORRECT today is rejected: it would drift the moment anything upstream moved, and it is the same category of claim D0 made

**R19** *a board rendered without the font* — FIRED. the page measures its own fingerprint against the serif fallback; equal widths mean every glyph is a fallback and the render exits non-zero

**R20** *the guard’s own history* — FIRED. this guard was added AFTER an over-full screen squeezed three panels without looking broken, and its first version measured the children instead of the container that clips them, so it reported 0 while the last panel was being cut off

**R21** *a saturation-slider "greyscale" instead of the WCAG transform* — FIRED. the transform is WCAG relative luminance applied to the PIXELS Chrome drew. Re-rendering the scene with desaturated tokens would only prove that a different scene looks different.

**R22** *a dichromacy board with no stated source* — FIRED. the check reads derivedFrom and fails when it is absent

**R23** *the two behavioural probes, neither of them invented* — FIRED. disabled-paint-without-the-attribute / outline-removed-with-no-replacement / discoverable-unavailable-that-still-activates / only-the-native-pattern-styled / the-override-taking-the-record-too — both are ordinary implementer mistakes, and both are rejected

**R24** *the defect this check actually caught* — FIRED. an earlier build styled only [data-state~="focus"], so every STILL painted a ring the real focus state never produced and the keyboard got Chrome’s 1px default outline. No still could have seen it.

**R31** *the three behavioural probes E1 could not have written, because it had ruled the pattern out of existence* — FIRED. FIRED discoverable-unavailable-that-still-activates · FIRED only-the-native-pattern-styled · FIRED the-override-taking-the-record-too — the first is the ordinary aria-disabled mistake: reachable, painted unavailable, fully operable

## 5. The behavioural proof

Real `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` Tab events through a real browser. A synthetic
`KeyboardEvent` constructed in page script carries no default action, so a Tab test
written in page JS measures its own `focus()` calls and always passes.

| obligation | result | detail |
|---|---|---|
| the tab ring visits every reachable control, in document order | **MET** | visited ["r1","r3","inp","o1","o2","o3","o4","b1","r4"] expected ["r1","r3","inp","o1","o2","o3","o4","b1","r4"] |
| a NATIVE NON-DISCOVERABLE unavailable control is skipped by the tab ring | **MET** | ["r2","b2"] carry the HTML disabled attribute; focus landed on neither |
| a DISCOVERABLE unavailable control REMAINS REACHABLE by the tab ring | **MET** | ["o3","o4"] carry aria-disabled and no disabled attribute; focus reached ["o3","o4"] — W3C APG: screen reader users are far less likely to discover disabled elements that are not focusable |
| every focused control paints the indicator at the resolved width | **MET** | widths ["2px"] expected 2px solid |
| the indicator is the resolved token colour, not a browser default | **MET** | saw ["rgb(216, 213, 202)"] expected rgb(216, 213, 202) |
| the indicator is DETACHED at the resolved offset | **MET** | offsets ["2px"] expected 2px |
| the dark companion is present outside the indicator | **MET** | box-shadow present on 10 of 10 |
| exactly one control carries the indicator at a time | **MET** | counted 1 |
| Shift+Tab returns to the previous control | **MET** | landed on r4 |
| the focus perimeter on an unavailable control is the focus token, NOT dimmed with the control | **MET** | o4 focused: rgb(216, 213, 202) at 2px — the perimeter belongs to the input system, and the input system is not unavailable (precedence rule P3) |
| an AVAILABLE control activates under a real Enter key | **MET** | focus landed on b1, which then activated 1 time(s) — without this the obligation below would be vacuous, because a key that activates nothing passes it |
| a DISCOVERABLE unavailable control CANNOT be activated by the same key | **MET** | o4 activated 0, o3 activated 0 — aria-disabled suppresses nothing on its own; MDN: "web developers must manually ensure such elements have their functionality suppressed" |
| the two availability patterns are VISUALLY IDENTICAL | **MET** | DISCOVERABLE o4 rgb(105, 103, 98) · NATIVE r2 rgb(105, 103, 98) · unavailable ink rgb(105, 103, 98) — a visible difference would encode an implementation decision as a Product meaning |
| SELECTED + UNAVAILABLE keeps the record of the choice and gives up only the ink | **MET** | o3 marker present true in rgb(105, 103, 98), weight 600 (selected weight is 600), ink rgb(105, 103, 98) — precedence rule P1: the availability override takes every ink INCLUDING the marker’s, and takes neither the marker’s presence nor the weight |
| SELECTED + UNAVAILABLE is distinguishable from UNAVAILABLE and from SELECTED | **MET** | against UNAVAILABLE o4: marker true vs false, weight 600 vs 500 · against SELECTED o2: ink rgb(105, 103, 98) vs rgb(216, 213, 202) |

**probe — disabled-paint-without-the-attribute:** FIRED. focus reached ["r2","b2"] — the skip obligation MUST reject this

**probe — outline-removed-with-no-replacement:** FIRED. every stop reported outline-style ["none"] — the visibility obligation MUST reject this

**probe — discoverable-unavailable-that-still-activates:** FIRED. o4 activated 1, o3 activated 1 — reachable, painted unavailable, and fully operable. The activation obligation MUST reject this

**probe — only-the-native-pattern-styled:** FIRED. DISCOVERABLE o4 rgb(139, 137, 130) vs NATIVE r2 rgb(105, 103, 98) — the visual-invariance obligation MUST reject this

**probe — the-override-taking-the-record-too:** FIRED. o3 marker present false, weight 500 vs plain UNAVAILABLE o4 weight 500 — SELECTED + UNAVAILABLE becomes indistinguishable from UNAVAILABLE and the user’s choice is silently rewritten

## 7. Cross-artefact consistency

`tools/e1-consistency.mjs` reads the **shipped artefacts back from disk** — 34
`.md` and `.json` files, with `vendor/` excluded because it is other packages' text and
must stay byte-identical. It does not read the source that wrote them and it does not read
rule text.

**A correction is not done until every generated surface agrees.** This guard earned its
place before it was finished: two surfaces — a token `$description` and a board caption —
were still carrying a claim E1 had already withdrawn when it was written.

| withdrawn claim | shipped anywhere? |
|---|---|
| REV-01 — disabled focusability frozen as a universal | no |
| REV-02 — the exclusivity rule about visual channels | no |
| REV-03 — the number of status hues frozen as a cap | no |
| the universal navigation and entitlement law E1 made | no |
| the reasoning that produced the universal law, restated as fact | no |
| the press wash proved by composited chroma | no |
| the C2/C3 restatement of the disabled collision, asserted rather than quoted | no |
| the state and status groups still described as empty | no |
| E1 described as adding two colours | no |
| tritanopia used as a derived floor | no |

The exact strings the guard matches on are in `tools/e1-consistency.mjs` and in
`data/E1_CONSISTENCY.json`, which is the one file the guard does not scan — a report
about withdrawn claims has to be able to name them.

Each needle is also fed a sentence that MUST be caught, so the guard is proved in both
directions: **10 / 10** probes fired.

And every headline figure a document states is checked against the JSON that produced it:
**9 / 9** agree.

- `32 / 32` — checks — agrees in 1 document(s)
- `32 / 32` — probes fired — agrees in 1 document(s)
- `15 / 15` — behavioural obligations — agrees in 1 document(s)
- `26` — dichromacy property tests — agrees in 2 document(s)
- `15` — boards — agrees in 1 document(s)
